subject: Astronomy & Space
title: Irregular Moons: Captured Wanderers
description: Learn Irregular Moons: Captured Wanderers in one minute.

hook.text: Most giant planets have dozens of small, distant moons on tilted or backward orbits. These are captured objects.

buildup.text: Jupiter has 95 known moons, Saturn 146. Most are irregulars—just a few kilometers wide, orbiting far from the planet.

discovery.text: Modern surveys keep finding more. Saturn surpassed Jupiter's moon count in 2023 when 62 new tiny moons were confirmed.

twist.text: Many irregulars form families—groups with similar orbits, likely fragments from a single captured object that broke apart.

climax.text: These moons are windows into the small-body population of the early solar system—captured billions of years ago.

punchline.text: Hundreds of captured moons. Broken fragments of ancient wanderers, still orbiting.

quiz.question: What are irregular moons?
options: Small moons on tilted or backward orbits, likely captured from elsewhere in the solar system
Moons that change shape as they orbit due to tidal forces
Moons that orbit in the exact same plane as their planet's rings

details.summary: Irregular moons are satellites in distant, eccentric, and often retrograde orbits — captured rather than formed with their planet. Jupiter has over 90 known moons, many irregular. Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune each have dozens.
details.whyItMatters: Irregular moons reveal how giant planets captured passing objects, sampling small body populations from across the solar system. They provide windows into the chaotic dynamical history of planetary migration.
takeaways: Satellites in distant, eccentric, or retrograde orbits
Captured rather than formed alongside their planet
Provide samples of the solar system's primordial small bodies

faq.question: How are irregular moons captured?
faq.answer: Three mechanisms: gas drag in the planet's early gas envelope slowed passing objects; three-body interactions where a binary asteroid encountered the planet and one member was captured; or dynamical friction during planetary migration.

faq.question: Why do irregular moons form families?
faq.answer: Many irregular moons cluster in groups with similar orbits, suggesting a single captured parent body that later broke apart through collisions. Jupiter's irregular moons form several distinct families.
